motion: Does consciousness fundamentally pervade reality and point toward God?

moves.currentDescription: The inanimate world and life form a continuum of responsiveness, with life greatly increasing the speed and extent of response.
moves.lockedProposition: The inanimate world and life form a continuum of responsiveness, with life greatly increasing the speed and extent of response.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: I used to think that there was a very hard line between inanimate matter and life. And there still is a very very important um line and a distinction, but it's not a hard and absolute one. So, I think that in some ways, even the inanimate world responds to things just in a very very very slow way. And what life does is massively increase both the speed and the uh amount of its responses. So, life is just vastly more responsive to changes in the environment than inanimacy. So, I think that there's a continuum there.
